title: Quiz — Chapter 2.2: Solving Inequalities Using Addition or Subtraction

questions.prompt: Which property of inequality allows you to add the same number to both sides?
questions.feedbackIfWrong: The Addition Property of Inequality allows adding the same number to both sides.
hints: The property name matches the operation.
It's the one that involves adding, not subtracting.
Look at the operation on x: subtraction.
questions.prompt: To solve $x - 6 \ge -10$, you must ___ 6 to both sides.
questions.feedbackIfWrong: Add 6 to both sides to isolate x.

questions.prompt: Solve $m - 3 \le 5$. What is the solution inequality? (e.g., m <= 8)

hints: ≥ means the boundary number is included.
questions.prompt: When graphing $x \ge -4$, you use a ___ circle at -4.
questions.feedbackIfWrong: A closed circle is used because -4 is included.

questions.prompt: Solve $-8 < 1.4 + m$. Write the solution with m on the left. (e.g., m > 5)
hints: Then rewrite so m is on the left, flipping the symbol.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is equivalent to $x - 2 > -9$?
Before solving $j + 9 - 3 < 8$, combine the constants 9 and -3 to get $j + ___ < 8$.
questions.feedbackIfWrong: 9 - 3 = 6, so the simplified inequality is j + 6 < 8.

questions.prompt: A circuit has a maximum of 1800 watts. A microwave uses 1100 watts. Write an inequality for the additional watts w you can add without overloading. (e.g., 1100 + w < 1800)
hints: The total must be less than the maximum.
Use the < symbol because overloading means strictly less than 1800.

hints: 'No more than 50' means 'less than or equal to 50'.
